claims.text: A DNN interatomic potential trained on high-temperature AIMD configurations can represent the configurational diversity of solid and liquid refractory high-entropy alloys better than traditional EAM references.
The DNN reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to EAM references.
Equimolar MoNbTaW is an applicable refractory high-entropy-alloy system for the proposed method.
The relevant temperature range for equimolar refractory HEAs is approximately 3000–3500 K, corresponding to 0.95–1.0 times the melting temperature.
An active-learning DNN potential can be trained from high-temperature AIMD configurations sampled in crystalline and liquid states.
Active learning will explicitly sample a broad spectrum of atomic configurations relevant to the target refractory HEA.
The method applies to both solid and liquid phases of equimolar refractory HEAs at 0.95–1.0 times their melting temperature.
The DNN encodes a high-dimensional, many-body potential-energy surface.
The DNN captures subtle liquid-state correlations that EAM potentials miss.
Training on diverse AIMD configurations from both phases yields a more accurate free-energy landscape.
A more accurate free-energy landscape improves phase-space overlap between the DNN reference and the ab initio target.
Improved phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to fixed-form EAM references.
The DNN reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
DNN-based free-energy differences will agree more closely with direct ab initio benchmarks than EAM-based results.
Traditional EAM potentials used in TOR-TILD underrepresent many-body liquid configurations and therefore produce larger thermodynamic-integration mismatches.
The benefit of the DNN reference will be most pronounced near the melting temperature.
Performance may degrade outside the training temperature or composition range.
Overfitting or failure to sample rare configurations may limit the DNN potential's accuracy and generalizability.
Failure to reduce mismatch by at least approximately 30% relative to the EAM control would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of DNN-derived free-energy differences to converge significantly closer to a direct AIMD benchmark would falsify the hypothesis.
